title: Empathy, sympathy and antipathy
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:13Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:42Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the distinction between empathy, sympathy and antipathy; the closest, Positioning the reader, covers steering reader feelings through word choice and detail but not these three named responses or the sharing-of-feelings idea, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: Empathy, sympathy and antipathy
card: sharing a character's feelings, as if you feel them with the character. A reader who tingles with nerves as a character waits to go on stage feels empathy.
feeling sorry for a character, while staying outside their feelings. A reader who thinks "that poor boy" about a lost child feels sympathy.
disliking a character. A reader who is annoyed by a character who mocks others feels antipathy.

Writers shape these responses through a character's choices and motives. A character who acts kindly for good reasons can draw empathy or sympathy. One who acts cruelly for selfish reasons can draw antipathy.
draft.remember: Empathy is feeling with a character, sympathy is feeling sorry for them, and antipathy is disliking them.

a.q: Ravi reads about a girl who is teased at school. He feels sorry for her, but he does not feel her hurt himself. Which response is this?
a.why: Feeling sorry for a character while staying outside their feelings is sympathy. Empathy is tempting, but it means sharing the feelings, not just feeling sorry.
a.clue: Is Ravi feeling the same hurt, or feeling sorry for her?

b.q: In a story, Dev lies to his friends to take the credit for a team win, and he does not feel bad about it. Which response is the writer most likely shaping in the reader?
opts: Antipathy, because of his selfish choice
Empathy, because he is the main character
Sympathy, because he is on the winning team
Empathy, because he is a young person
b.why: Dev's choice to lie for credit shows a selfish motive, which draws a reader to dislike him. Being the main character does not on its own make a reader share his feelings. The writer shapes the response through his choices and motives.
b.clue: Look at what Dev chooses to do and why.

b.best: Antipathy, because of his selfish choice
